title: Bioparticle Microarrays for Chemotactic and Molecular Analysis of Human Neutrophil Swarming in vitro
protocol: Generate the master silicon wafer using standard photolithography procedures.
Use computer-aided design (CAD) software to create the desired design.
Send the design to a photomask manufacturer for production of a chrome photomask.
Spincoat a 40 µm thick layer of negative photoresist onto a silicon wafer.
Bake the wafer at 65 °C for 5 min and then at 95 °C for 10 min.
Expose the wafer to UV light through the chrome photomask with 150–160 mJ/cm².
Bake the wafer again at 65 °C for 5 min and then at 95 °C for 10 min.
Submerge the wafer in photoresist developer for 10 min, followed by rinsing with isopropyl alcohol.
Thoroughly mix a 10:1 ratio of polydimethylsiloxane prepolymer and its curing agent (20 g prepolymer and 2 g curing agent).
Pour the uncured PDMS mixture over the master wafer in a Petri dish.
Vacuum treat the uncured PDMS mixture until no air bubbles are present over the master wafer.
Cure the treated PDMS at 65 °C overnight.
Cut around the exterior of the patterned section of the wafer with a scalpel to remove the cured PDMS slab.
Place the PDMS slab on a clean cutting board with the patterned side facing up.
Punch out individual stamps from the PDMS slab using an 8 mm biopsy punch.
Place each stamp face down on adhesive tape to remove any debris.
Prepare a 1.6 mg/mL solution of CP in water by adding the proper amount of CP powder (e.g., 0.8 g) to water (500 mL).
Mix the CP powder and water on a stir plate at room temperature overnight, or until all solid is dissolved.
Aliquot about 10 mL of the CP solution for use.
Add 0.05 mg of PLL-FITC to the aliquoted volume of CP solution.
Vortex the CP solution labeled with FITC for 20 s, ensuring a uniform, pale yellow color.
Protect the fluorescent CP solution from light and store at 4 °C for up to 1 month.
Prime each stamp with 100 µL of 1.6 mg/mL solution of CP, ensuring no air bubbles form between the CP solution and the stamp.
Invert stamps onto a layer of CP solution.
Remove stamps from the CP solution after 1 hour.
Dab each wet stamp face down on a clean glass slide 6-8 times.
Vacuum treat the stamps for 1-2 minutes.
Adhere an eight-well, 9 mm diameter imaging spacer on top of a clean glass slide as a guide for stamp placement.
Place a stamp face down on the glass slide in the center of each well of the imaging spacer.
Place a 5.6 ± 0.1 g balanced weight on top of each stamp and allow 10 minutes for stamping.
Remove weights and stamps from the glass slide.
Allow the CP layer to dry at room temperature for 24 hours before adding bioparticles.
Cut a blank PDMS slab to the size of the imaging spacer.
Create wells in the PDMS that align with the wells of an imaging spacer using an 8 mm biopsy punch.
Adhere the PDMS slab to the glass slide with the imaging spacer.
Thaw a solution of bioparticles and dilute to 500 μg/mL in water for injection (WFI).
Add 100 μL of bioparticle solution to each PDMS well on the glass slide.
Rock the glass slide for 30 min.
Rinse the wells thoroughly with water.
Separate red blood cells (RBCs) by adding an erythrocyte aggregation agent in a 1:5 ratio to the whole blood.
Wait 45 min for a translucent layer (buffy coat) to separate from the layer of RBCs.
Remove the buffy coat and wash with phosphate buffered saline (PBS) using 1 mL buffy coat: 9 mL PBS.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 190 x g and 20 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet at 5 x 10^7 cells/mL.
Add 50 μL of antibody cocktail/1 mL cell suspension.
Wait 10 min.
Add 100 μL of magnetic beads/1 mL cell suspension.
Wait 10 min.
Add cell suspension to a round-bottom tube and place in a cylindrical magnet.
Wait 10 min.
Pour supernatant into a centrifuge tube.
Add up to 10 mL of PBS.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 190 x g and 20 °C.
Aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend white pellet in IMDM with 0.4% human serum albumin.
Stain nuclei with 20 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 for 10 min at 37 °C.
Add 5 mL of IMDM with 0.4% human serum albumin to rinse.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 190 x g and 20 °C.
Resuspend cells at 7.5 x 10^5 cells/mL in IMDM with 0.4% human serum albumin.
Add 100 µL of the cell suspension to a PDMS well containing a bioparticle microarray.
Ensure the cell suspension is convex over the top of the PDMS well and does not contain any bubbles.
Seal with a 12 mm diameter coverslip.
Cover the opening of the PDMS well with a 12 mm diameter coverslip.
Press down gently onto the coverslip with tweezers so the excess cell suspension escapes to the edge of the well.
Use a tissue to remove the excess cell suspension.
Load microparticle array with cells on the live cell imaging station with a microscope equipped with a cage incubator set to 37 °C, 5% CO2, and 90% relative humidity.
Use time-lapse fluorescent and brightfield microscopy to record images at 10x magnification every 10 s at 405 nm, 594 nm, and brightfield.
Use an automated cell tracking software to track individual neutrophil migration toward a bioparticle cluster.
Set the spot radius in the autoregression mode of the cell tracking software to 5 μm.
Set the minimum track length to 120 s and maximum gap size to one frame.
Extract files from the data generated by the cell tracking software containing neutrophil position and speed.
Use graphing software to generate neutrophil migration tracks and a heat map of speed vs. time.
Use 405 nm fluorescent images to track swarm size over time on an image analysis software.
Define regions of interest (ROIs) around each bioparticle cluster where neutrophils will swarm, keeping the same ROI size for all clusters.
Analyze mean fluorescent intensity of the 405 nm images within each ROI over time.
Generate a calibration curve of mean fluorescent intensity to swarm size by taking manual measurements from 0 µm² to maximum swarm size.
Use the calibration curve to calculate swarm size over time.
Incubate the neutrophils in the wells containing the bioparticle microarray at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 3 h.
Take samples at desired time points.
Typically, take samples at 0, 0.5, 1, and 3 h.
Use a brightfield microscope to verify that swarms are formed on the microarray.
Aspirate the supernatant with a 200 µL pipette.
Load the aspirated supernatant in a 0.45 μm centrifuge filter tube.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 190 x g and 20 °C for 5 min.
Collect the filtrated volume after centrifugation.
Store samples at -80 °C until processing time.
Add 200 µL of each sample to a separate dialysis tube provided with the kit.
Place the dialysis tubes in a beaker containing at least 500 mL of PBS (pH = 8.0).
Stir gently on a stir plate for at least 3 h at 4 °C.
Change the PBS in the beaker and repeat this step.
Transfer each sample to a clean centrifuge tube after dialysis.
Centrifuge at 9,000 x g for 5 min to remove any precipitates.
Transfer each supernatant to a clean tube.
Biotinylate each sample by adding 36 µL of 1x labeling reagent from the kit per 1 mg of total protein in the dialyzed sample to 180 µL of dialyzed sample.
Incubate at 20 °C for 30 min.
Mix gently every 5 min.
Add 3 µL of stop solution into each sample tube.
Transfer each sample to a fresh dialysis tube.
Store the sample at -20 °C or -80 °C until ready to proceed.
Allow the glass slide to come to room temperature.
Place the assembled glass slide in a laminar flow hood for 1–2 h at room temperature.
Add 400 μL of blocking buffer into each well of the assembled glass slide.
Incubate at room temperature for 30 min.
Centrifuge the prepared samples for 5 min at 9,000 x g to remove precipitates or particulates.
Dilute the samples 5x with blocking buffer.
Remove the blocking buffer from each well.
Add 400 μL of diluted samples into appropriate wells.
Incubate for 2 h at room temperature while rocking.
Decant the samples from each well.
Wash each well 3x with 800 µL of 1x wash buffer I at room temperature for 5 min each while rocking.
Submerge the assembled glass slide in 1x wash buffer I in a clean container.
Wash the assembled glass slide 2x at room temperature for 5 min each while rocking.
Add 400 μL of 1x Cy3-conjugated streptavidin to each sub-array.
Cover with plastic adhesive strips.
Incubate for 2 h at room temperature while rocking.
Decant the solution and disassemble the glass slide from the sample chambers.
Add the glass slide to a 30 mL centrifuge tube along with enough 1x wash buffer I to cover it.
Wash the glass slide three times for 10 minutes each at room temperature while rocking.
Wash the glass slide twice with 1x wash buffer II for 5 minutes each at room temperature while rocking.
Wash the glass slide with 30 mL of ddH2O for 5 minutes.
Remove the glass slide from the centrifuge tube and allow it to dry for 20 minutes in a laminar flow hood.
Store the prepared glass slide at -20 °C until ready to scan.
